item.title: The Daily Dirt: Mamdani shows signs of weakness
item.description: Vulnerabilities have begun to appear in Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s armor. The property tax proposal was the biggest. item.title: Bad connection: Dish Wireless stiffs landlords
item.description: Cliff Steinberg has good relationships with all his tenants, except one: Dish Wireless. Steinberg is the landlord at Manhattan’s 161 Lafayette Street, a fully commercial building with about seven tenants. But a few months ago, Dish Wireless, which put a cell tower on the roof in 2022, stopped paying its rent. “There’s no one to talk to. No one returns your calls,” Steinberg said of Dish. “It’s dead.” It’s a story that’s unfolding across New York, in multifamily as well as commercial buildings. C

item.title: Amstar acquires Hudson Yards rental tower for $129M
item.description: Denver-based Amstar Group is acquiring a Hudson Yards luxury rental building, which appears to be its first venture into New York’s multifamily market. Amstar agreed to buy the 33-story, 225-unit Henry Hall property at 515 West 38th Street for $129 million, Bloomberg reported. The deal works out to $573,000 per unit. item.description: Astoria’s building boom isn’t cooling off and Schuman Properties wants a bigger piece of it. item.title: BRP Companies sells Long Island rental complex for $190M
item.description: Two years after opening, a luxury multifamily complex in a Long Island hamlet is already changing hands. An affiliate of the Illinois-based Inland Real Estate Group of Companies purchased The Arboretum in Farmingville for $190 million, JLL announced. The seller was BRP Companies and the deal for the 292-unit property pencils out to $651,000 per unit. item.title: Metropole’s 681 Fifth Ave sells for $100K … with a “K”
item.description: A Tuesday foreclosure auction brought a paltry sale for Fifth Avenue property tied to Robert Siegel’s Metropole Realty Advisors. It may not be the saga’s final chapter, though. Metropole’s 681 Fifth Avenue sold at auction for a measly $100,000, Crain’s reported. item.title: City Urban snags Soho corner lot at steep discount
item.description: City Urban Realty snapped up one of Soho’s last blank canvases. Michael Alvandi’s firm paid $14 million for a vacant corner lot at 144 Spring Street in an off-market deal, The Real Deal has learned. The price is a steep discount from the $24.7 million that Travelzoo founder Ralph Bartel paid for the property in 2012.
